## 1. Rejection source: NOT in this repo — t-agents is a CONSUMER of llm-proxy

- Binary-safe search (`grep -rain -a`) for "Malicious MCP", "Invalid tools", "Security Guardrail", "guardrail", "critical data", "anon", "mask" across the whole repo: **zero hits for the guardrail strings**. The only "anon" matches are `Canonicalize` (`internal/verify/verify.go`), the only "mask" match is a port mask in `internal-docs/security/decisions/0012-jetbrains-mcp.md:24`, the only "malicious" hits are threat-model prose in `internal-docs/security/baseline/requirements.md:30-34`.
- This repo is **tclaude** — a Go launcher that wraps Claude Code and points ALL LLM traffic at the corp proxy:
  - `internal/run/bootstrap.go:18` — `const llmProxyBaseURL = "https://llm-proxy.t-tech.team"`; `bootstrap.go:85` sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to it.
  - `build/scripts/run.sh:38` — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://llm-proxy.t-tech.team"`.
  - `build/cc-config/managed-settings.json:75` and `internal-docs/security/baseline/managed-settings.json:136` — same env, signed managed config.
- The check's owner is the **llm-proxy service itself**, whose code is NOT in this repo. The repo names its function explicitly — `internal-docs/security/baseline/requirements.md:112`: «LLM-доступ: через корпоративный `https://llm-proxy.t-tech.team` (PII masking, prompt-injection guard). Прямой egress к Anthropic не блокируется sandbox'ом на v0 — контролируется командой Сеть.» The measured error's nesting ("failed to detect critical data: fail anon mask critical data: anon error") matches that PII-masking/anonymization ("anon") stage — the tool-name guardrail fires inside llm-proxy's critical-data-detection pipeline, before the request reaches Anthropic.
- `internal-docs/security/traceability.md:30` row 10: «LLM-доступ только через `llm-proxy.t-tech.team` | 🔄 | _TODO ADR_» — even the ADR for the proxy contract is unwritten; no proxy-side spec exists in this repo.
- Auth to the proxy: `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (`internal/apikey/apikey.go:4-25` — «рабочая авторизация к корп-прокси»; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` deliberately scrubbed), token issued via **ai-seats** «выдаётся через руководителя» (`docs/faq.md:106`, `docs/index.md:33`).

## 2. The allowlist(s) — what this repo defines (client-side) vs what it does not (proxy-side)

The proxy's server-side tool allowlist is **not defined anywhere in this repo**. What the repo defines is tclaude's own client-side trust boundary, which is the best available picture of "the corp-approved tool surface" that the proxy presumably mirrors:

- **MCP servers** (`build/cc-config/managed-settings.json:3-…`, `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` + `allowedMcpServers`): stdio `dp ai mcp <name>` for `jira`, `gitlab`, `wixie`, `tracker`, `finedog`, `sage`, `allure`; remote `context7` by `serverUrl` `https://mcp.context7.com/*`; plus JetBrains IDE on `127.0.0.1:6434*` (ADR-0012). Fixed by `internal-docs/security/decisions/0001-mcp-allowlist.md` (Accepted 2026-06-25): «При `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` … deny-by-default: любой сервер, которого нет в списке, не загружается» (lines 15-17); user cannot extend it (line 37). User-facing table: `docs/mcp-setup.md:19-31`.
- **Native Claude Code tools** are governed by permission rules, not an allowlist: `permissions.ask` (WebFetch, WebSearch, `git push` etc.) and a large `permissions.deny` in `build/cc-config/managed-settings.json`.
- **Per-tool MCP denials** in that same deny list are the key naming evidence: `mcp__wixie__dp_wixie_comments`, `mcp__gitlab__dp_gitlab_create-merge-request`, `mcp__gitlab__dp_gitlab_fork`, `mcp__gitlab__dp_gitlab_whoami`, `mcp__allure__dp_allure_*` (9 entries). So the corp-blessed wire names are `mcp__<short-server>__dp_<server>_<tool>` — server segment `gitlab`, not `dpGitlab`.
- **Skills/plugins**: `internal-docs/security/baseline/skills-allowlist.json` (static corp skill list), `plugins-allowlist.json` — «empty allowlist + `third_party_llm_plugins: true` в denylist» (requirements.md:149).
- Directly relevant to the measured 403: **Nessy's `mcp__dpGitlab__dp_gitlab_create-merge-request` differs from the corp-approved name `mcp__gitlab__dp_gitlab_create-merge-request` only in the server segment** — the same underlying dp integration fails the proxy guard purely by wire-name mismatch. `mcp__session__*`, `mcp__plugin_figma_figma__*` have no corp counterpart at all. (Inference from naming evidence; the proxy's actual list is unverifiable from repo A.)

## 3. Matching rule

Not determinable from this repo — the guardrail code is absent. What the repo supports:

- The measured error enumerates each offending tool by full name, consistent with **per-name lookup against an allowed set**, not a blanket `mcp__*` ban (tclaude's whole fleet runs `mcp__gitlab__*`/`mcp__jira__*` daily through this same proxy, per the managed config — a categorical `mcp__*` block would break the shipped product).
- Why chat-completions passes: no evidence in repo A. The repo only wires the **Anthropic path** (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`); it never touches an OpenAI-compatible route on llm-proxy. Most plausible reading (flagged as inference, matches your measurement): the critical-data/anon guard with tool inspection is middleware on the `/v1/messages` pipeline only, and the chat-completions pipeline either lacks the tool check or has a different one. Confirming requires the llm-proxy service repo, which this clone does not contain.

## 4. Registration process for new tools/integrations

- **tclaude's own allowlist** has a documented change route: ADR journal `internal-docs/security/decisions/README.md` («журнал согласований … после согласования с ИБ»); ADR-0001:45-46: «При изменении перечня — обновить этот ADR (или выпустить замещающий) и пересобрать/переподписать `managed-settings.json`»; `docs/how-it-works.md:145`: «Изменение политики выполняется исключительно по этому маршруту: правка исходника → `make build` → `sudo tclaude install` … Предложения по правилам направляйте в [~nestor-ask]»; `docs/local-overrides.md:136`: «После согласования с ИБ → правило переносится в базовый профиль».
- **llm-proxy's guardrail allowlist**: NO registration process documented in this repo. The entry points the repo gives for anything proxy-related: support channel **`~nestor-ask`** (`https://time.tbank.ru/tinkoff/channels/nestor-ask` — `docs/faq.md:7`, `docs/index.md:38`), network access form `https://my.tbank.ru/access/mall/vpn` for `llm-proxy.t-tech.team:443` (`docs/faq.md:48-53`), tokens via ai-seats. Traceability row 10's `_TODO ADR_` confirms the proxy contract is not yet written down. The deferred conversation's entry point is therefore the llm-proxy owners via ~nestor-ask (and the ИБ ADR round if the fix is to be codified), not anything in t-agents.

BOTTOM LINE: t-agents does not own the guardrail; llm-proxy.t-tech.team does (its "anon"/PII-masking stage). Repo A's only tool allowlists are client-side signed managed-config; their naming (`mcp__gitlab__dp_gitlab_*` etc.) is the likely template for the proxy's allowed set, which is why Nessy's `mcp__dpGitlab__*`/`mcp__session__*`/`mcp__plugin_*` names 403 on the Anthropic path.

## TASK 2 — Why our claude-runtime tool names differ from native Claude Code

### (1) What NATIVE Claude Code sends on the wire

Source: the bundled `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.218` (`node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk-tools.d.ts`, `ToolInputSchemas` union) — this IS the binary our claude-runtime spawns, so its surface is the native baseline.

Native built-in names (sent bare, no prefix): `Agent` (the subagent tool — renamed from `Task`; the repo already shipped a bug from that rename, see AGENTS.md), `Bash`, `TaskOutput`, `TaskStop`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `NotebookEdit`, `TodoWrite` (upstream-disabled by default since CLI v2.1.142 per `tools-reference.md:57`, cited at `session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1320-1324`), `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `AskUserQuestion`, `EnterPlanMode`, `ExitPlanMode`, `TaskCreate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskList`, `ListMcpResources`, `ReadMcpResource`, `ReadMcpResourceDir`, `RefreshMcpTools`, `Mcp`, `ReportFindings`, `SendFeedback`, `CronCreate`, `CronDelete`, `CronList`, `ScheduleWakeup`, `Monitor`, `RemoteTrigger`, `EnterWorktree`, `ExitWorktree`, `PushNotification`, `REPL`, `Workflow`, `ClaudeDesign`, `Projects`, `Artifact`, `ProposeSkills`, `ShowOnboardingRolePicker` (which subset is live per turn is the CLI's own gating — env flags, feature state).

MCP tools in native Claude Code: `mcp__<serverName>__<toolName>` for user/project/local servers; `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<toolName>` for plugin-bundled servers (`mcp.md:357`, `mcp.md:365` — quoted verbatim in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-stable-plugin-mcp-wire-names.md`). **So `mcp__`-prefixed names are not a Nessy invention — they are Claude Code's own convention for every MCP tool.**

### (2) What OUR claude-runtime session sends, and where names are minted

`packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1286-1454` builds the turn:

- **SDK built-ins ride natively**: `tools: { type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code' }` (line 1448-1454) — the same native surface as stock Claude Code — minus `disallowedTools: ['EnterPlanMode', 'ExitPlanMode', 'AskUserQuestion', 'Skill']` (line 1291), with the design comment: *"Block SDK tools that require UI we don't have: EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode: We use safe mode instead (user-controlled via UI); AskUserQuestion: Requires interactive UI to show question options to user."*
- **Session tools ride as an in-process SDK MCP server named `session`** (`claude-agent.ts:1309-1311` → `getSessionScopedTools` in `packages/shared/src/agent/session-scoped-tools.ts:209-335`, `createSdkMcpServer({ name: 'session', … })` at line 330). The SDK mints the wire name `mcp__session__<tool>`. **Why MCP, not native names: the Claude Agent SDK's only extension point for host-executed custom tools is `createSdkMcpServer`/`tool()` — there is no API to register a bare-named built-in.** The file header (lines 1-16) states the design: session-tools-core is the canonical cross-runtime registry (Pi, Claude, Codex, session-mcp-server all consume it; "Tool visibility is centrally filtered in session-tools-core to avoid backend drift", line 277-278), and the Claude file is "a thin adapter that wraps the shared handlers … for use with the Claude SDK".
- **Source/dp/plugin MCPs ride as per-source proxy servers** (`claude-agent.ts:558-618`): *"The SDK adds its own `mcp__{serverKey}__` prefix, so we use the source slug as the server key and original tool names to get the correct final names (e.g., `mcp__linear__createIssue`)."* Pool slugs = wire names minted by the one naming authority (`applyCollisionPolicy` in `capabilities/resolver.ts` per the wire-names plan): builtin dp servers keep bare catalogue names (`dpGitlab`, `dpJira` — `packages/shared/src/mcp/builtin-dp-servers.ts:115-116`), plugin servers ALWAYS get `plugin_<pluginId>_<serverName>` — an owner decision from the 2026-08-10 lane, adopting **Claude Code's own contract** so "correctly-written Claude plugins' internal references match without translation".

Claude-visible `mcp__session__*` set (default projection of `SESSION_TOOL_DEFS`, pi-only filtered out, `tool-defs.ts:1308-1341`): `SubmitPlan, config_validate, skill_validate, mermaid_validate, source_test, source_manage, source_oauth_trigger, source_google_oauth_trigger, source_credential_prompt, update_user_preferences, remember, TodoWrite, transform_data, script_sandbox, render_template, send_developer_feedback, SlashCommand, BashOutput, ProcessStop, set_session_labels, set_session_status, get_session_info, list_sessions, read_skill_resource, automation_list, automation_validate, automation_create, automation_update, send_agent_message, plugin_plan_install, plugin_install, plugin_status, plugin_manage, ReportFindings, SendUserFile` + backend-added `call_llm, spawn_session` + `browser_tool` family — ~38 tools.

### (3) Delta table — native name vs what we send

| Function | Native Claude Code | Our claude-runtime | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| File/exec/search core | `Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch` | **identical** (preset) | no delta |
| Subagents | `Agent` | **identical** | no delta |
| Background shells | `TaskOutput`, `TaskStop` | identical, PLUS `mcp__session__BashOutput`/`mcp__session__ProcessStop` (host-owned background processes, cross-runtime contract) | duplication by design |
| Todo checklist | `TodoWrite` (upstream-disabled by default) / `TaskCreate/Get/Update/List` | natives present per preset, PLUS `mcp__session__TodoWrite` — its handler writes the todo-state file the desktop UI plates render (`handlers/todo-write.ts`) | UI needs host-side state |
| Plan mode | `EnterPlanMode`/`ExitPlanMode` | **disallowed** → `mcp__session__SubmitPlan` + host safe-mode UI | comment at `claude-agent.ts:1288` |
| Ask user | `AskUserQuestion` | **disallowed** (no SDK-side UI) | comment at 1289 |
| Skills | `Skill` | **disallowed**; skills surface via capability context + `mcp__session__read_skill_resource` | |
| Slash commands | `SlashCommand` | `mcp__session__SlashCommand` → host `dispatchSlashCommandFn` (commands live host-side, cross-runtime) | |
| Review findings | `ReportFindings` | both possible: native + `mcp__session__ReportFindings` | |
| User MCP source (e.g. linear) | `mcp__linear__createIssue` | **identical** (`mcp__<slug>__<tool>`) | same convention |
| dp builtins | `mcp__dpGitlab__dp_gitlab_*` (if user configured same server name) | **identical shape** | bare-name mint |
| Plugin MCPs | `mcp__plugin_figma_figma__download_assets` | **byte-identical** | Claude-parity mint, owner decision 2026-08-10 |
| No native equivalent AT ALL | — | `mcp__session__`: `SubmitPlan, config_validate, skill_validate, mermaid_validate, source_test, source_manage, source_oauth_trigger, source_google_oauth_trigger, source_credential_prompt, update_user_preferences, remember, transform_data, script_sandbox, render_template, send_developer_feedback, set_session_labels, set_session_status, get_session_info, list_sessions, read_skill_resource, automation_*, send_agent_message, plugin_plan_install/install/status/manage, SendUserFile, call_llm, spawn_session`, `browser_tool` family | Nessy product features |

**Key finding for the owner:** the guardrail's "invalid" list is NOT mostly Nessy-divergent names. `mcp__dpGitlab__*` and `mcp__plugin_figma_figma__*` are exactly what a stock Claude Code with the same MCP config would send — the wire-name lane deliberately adopted Claude's contract. The only Nessy-specific names are the `mcp__session__*` family (the server key `session` is ours) and `browser_*` tool segments. So "match native Claude" cannot make the 403 go away: native Claude with any MCP server also emits `mcp__*` names, and the platform guardrail is evidently rejecting MCP tool names not on its allowlist, not detecting deviation from Claude's surface.

### (4) Alignment options — tradeoffs, no recommendation

**(a) Rename/bridge session tools to native-looking names.**
- The SDK cannot do it: `mcp__<server>__` is minted inside the SDK; an SDK MCP tool can never appear bare. The only seam is the per-session loopback adapter the claude-runtime already owns (`packages/shared/src/agent/backend/internal/drivers/anthropic.ts` + `@nessy-agent/codex-responses-adapter`) — rewrite tool names in the outgoing `/v1/messages` body and reverse-map `tool_use` blocks in responses.
- What breaks: (i) **collisions** — `TodoWrite`, `SlashCommand`, `ReportFindings`, would collide with the SDK's own built-ins of the same name (both present in one `tools` array = API error or ambiguous dispatch; reverse-mapping a bare `TodoWrite` back is ambiguous between the native tool and ours); (ii) ~27 session tools have **no native name to rename to** (`source_manage`, `call_llm`, `spawn_session`, `automation_*`, …) — the allowlist still rejects them, so renaming alone cannot pass the guardrail; (iii) permission scoping builds patterns on `mcp__<slug>__` (`permissions-config.ts:1271,1305`), UI parsers strip `mcp__session__` (`packages/ui/src/lib/tool-parsers.ts:433`, `SessionManager.ts:19725`), hooks/skill `allowed-tools` translation and transcripts all carry the current names — a wire-only rewrite keeps those intact, but any deeper rename breaks them and past transcripts; (iv) the rewrite layer becomes a permanent maintenance seam on every SDK upgrade (this repo has already shipped two production bugs from upstream tool renames).
- Buys: at most the ~10 overlap names look native; the other ~28 still fail the allowlist.

**(b) Register our names in the platform allowlist (owner-side conversation).**
- Zero app-code cost. What to register: `mcp__session__<tool>` — a **finite, stable, host-controlled list** (~38 names, enumerated above; the registry is the single mint, so the list is auditable); `mcp__dp<Name>__*` — finite (~30 builtin dp servers, catalogue in `builtin-dp-servers.ts`); `browser_*`.
- What does NOT fit a static list: user BYO sources (`mcp__<slug>__<tool>`, slug is user-chosen) and marketplace plugins (`mcp__plugin_<id>_<server>__<tool>`, unbounded). Those need a **pattern rule** (prefix/regex) or stay broken — and note native Claude Code has the identical problem, so the platform will face this for any Claude Code user, not just Nessy.
- Risk: allowlist churn every time a session tool is added; per-environment drift between what the app ships and what the proxy admits (403 mid-release).

**(c) Hybrid.**
- Keep preset natives as-is (already native). Register the finite sets (`mcp__session__*`, dp builtins) as exact names; negotiate a pattern rule for `mcp__plugin_*` and user slugs; optionally trim the Claude-path session surface (the mini-agent filter mechanism at `claude-agent.ts:1318-1322` already exists as precedent for serving a reduced `mcpServers` set) to shrink the registered list.
- Cost: a policy conversation plus possibly a "lean session surface" config; no wire rewriting, no collision risk, transcripts/permissions untouched.
- Residual risk: same churn as (b) but on a smaller list; plugin/user-source pattern rule weakens the guardrail's "known tools only" posture — that tradeoff is the platform owner's to price.

Orthogonal fact worth carrying into the owner conversation: the same list passes over chat-completions on the same host+key, so the guardrail is Anthropic-path-specific policy, not a general tool-name policy — aligning names in the app cannot be the whole fix by construction, because ~28 of our tools have no native-name form at all and plugin/user MCP names are already native-form and still rejected.

**Key files:** `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts` (1286-1454 turn assembly; 558-618 source proxies), `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/agent/session-scoped-tools.ts` (session server mint), `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts` (canonical registry + visibility filter), `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/mcp/builtin-dp-servers.ts` (dp wire names), `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-stable-plugin-mcp-wire-names.md` (Claude-parity naming contract + owner decisions), `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk-tools.d.ts` (native surface, v0.3.218), `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/agent/permissions-config.ts` + `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/ui/src/lib/tool-parsers.ts` (rename blast radius).
